questions.question: What does Part 2 of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus say if $F$ is an antiderivative of $f$ on $[a,b]$?
questions.explanation: If $F'=f$ on $[a,b]$, FTC2 evaluates $\int_a^b f=F(b)-F(a)$.
questions.source_support: The theorem states that if $F$ is an antiderivative of $f$ on $[a,b]$, then $\int_a^b f(x)\,\mathrm{d}x = F(b)-F(a)$.
